stemMd: A scientist writes: Repeating an experiment with a different method can be especially informative. Agreement may reduce concern that the result arose from a peculiarity of the original instrument. What is the main reason offered for using a different method?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It can test whether the result depends on a method-specific artefact.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It removes the need to state a hypothesis.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It avoids collecting any new data.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It guarantees every earlier conclusion was false.

explanationMd: A different method brings different potential biases. Agreement across methods therefore weakens the explanation that the original finding was solely an instrument-specific artefact, without proving absolute certainty.

distractorRationale.e: Agreement would not support that claim.
distractorRationale.b: The value comes from their differences.
distractorRationale.c: The hypothesis still guides the test.
